messages:
ravi: heads up — after the gpu-operator rollout in us-west-2 at ~02:12 UTC we're seeing a cluster-wide scheduling cascade. lots of GPU pods stuck Pending and nodes reporting driver-unavailable taint
megan: where are the errors showing up? kubelet? device-plugin?
zheng: quick dump from one affected node:
```
kubectl describe node ip-10-0-2-31 | egrep -A3 'Allocatable|Taints'
Allocatable:
  nvidia.com/gpu: 0
Taints:
  driver-unavailable:NoSchedule
```
ravi: kube-scheduler tries to place, then kubelet rejects because device-plugin advertised GPUs but /dev/nvidia* not present
ana: infra-bot shows the gpu-operator daemonset rolled to v1.6.3 at 02:12:07 UTC, bump from 1.6.1
infra-bot: gpu-operator rollout: gpu-operator/gpu-operator v1.6.3 -> SUCCESS in us-west-2 (canary then all)
megan: logs from one device-plugin pod:
```
E0421 02:14:19.123456   1 deviceplugin.go:234] Advertised device path not found: /dev/nvidia0
E0421 02:14:19.123467   1 deviceplugin.go:256] failing advertise: driver not ready
```
zheng: and dmesg from node shows dkms probe failures and kernel symbol mismatches (kernel 5.15.* headers vs module built for 5.10):
```
nvidia: Failed to load module, unresolved symbol: nvkm_init
DKMS build for nvidia failed: kernel headers mismatch
```
megan: sounds like the operator triggered a driver module recompile that failed on some host kernels -> device plugin advertised prematurely -> scheduler backpressure -> pods pending
tom: also seeing NCCL errors in the app logs (peer detect failing), so even after partial node re-registration, multi-GPU jobs degrade: "NCCL WARN PeerToPeer: failed to setup p2p link"
ravi: impact: throughput drop ~40% on MPI jobs and a temporary capacity reduction (allocatable GPUs 0 -> spike in queuing). cost implications: longer runtime on spot fleets and retries = extra spend
ana: proposed immediate mitigations:
- cordon affected nodepools + taint to keep scheduler from reattempting
- rollback gpu-operator to 1.6.1 image in us-west-2 canary first
- restart nvidia-device-plugin daemonset on nodes after ensuring driver modules present
megan: commands I'm about to run (canary on 2 nodes):
```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-2-31
kubectl taint node ip-10-0-2-31 driver-unavailable=true:NoSchedule
kubectl set image ds/gpu-operator gpu-operator=redwood/gpu-operator:1.6.1 -n gpu-system --record
kubectl rollout restart ds nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset -n gpu-system
```
zheng: dev note for follow-up: device-plugin should probe /proc/driver/nvidia/version and /dev/nvidia* before advertising; add a short backoff + retry loop to avoid advertise-before-probe races when DKMS rebuilds are happening
megan: rolled back operator image on canary pool at 02:25, devices now re-registering, allocatable back to expected values on two nodes
ravi: verifying NCCL regressions still — one job shows peer detect fallback to ring over TCP, need deeper check if that was operator change or driver ABI mismatch
tom: opened INF-2042 to track full RCA + perf regression check and mitigation playbook (includes rollbacks, taint strategy, and device-plugin patch). tagging oncall for postmortem
ana: :thumbsup: nice containment. Next actions: run kernel header audit across fleets, add preflight check in rollout pipeline to validate module build for common kernel versions, and schedule a controlled operator upgrade in non-prod first
megan: agreed. I'll push a small hotfix to device-plugin that checks for /dev/nvidia* before Register() and add a 10s backoff. will PR and link INF-2042
ravi: thanks team — keeping this thread for recovery timeline updates. once stable we'll do a short postmortem and update rollout gating.
